description: Whether a result's receipt (an Ed25519 signature) seals exactly that request and that result, and every rule of its form holds (`reasons` names what does not). Pass the job's own `request` (as run_quantum_circuit or get_quantum_job returns it: a run here asks for its verdict, so the request it seals says so) and its result.

job.description: The job's text as it was given (preferred), or the job as an object. Either is read as the protocol reads a job's text, the job itself (or its members, given as this call's arguments) as this call writes it, so a member named twice or a whole number past a double is seen; `given` in the answer says which was judged

method.description: The body's method as the host gave it: unsealed, and noted where it differs from what is sealed

status.description: The body's status as the host gave it: unsealed, and noted where it differs from what is sealed

name: verify_quantum_receipt

anyOf.description: Whether a result's receipt seals exactly that request and that result and every rule of its form holds, and the key it names.

answer.description: For a job whose result seals the engine's verdict of its answer (the provider protocol's section 8.9): the verdict worked out again here. Its level, whether it holds, the layer that decided it with that layer's limits, the result's accuracy class, and again: reproduced, partly, host_statement (nothing of it could be worked out again here: it is the host's statement under its seal) or differs (not the verdict the job bears out: the job is then not valid, though its seal holds).

compile.description: For a sealed compile, or a job that ran compiled and carries its certificate's chain (wai/extensions/quantum-compile.md section 6): what a second look at the certificate found. again is reproduced (compiled again here, the request gives this certificate byte for byte), partly (not reproduced; the output was held to the program here by a tableau, in exact arithmetic or on dense unitaries, and whole says which), host_statement (its form holds, and nothing more could be decided here) or differs (not the certificate the request bears out: the job is then not valid, though its seal holds; differences says why).

form.description: chained: every pass names its digests, its layer and its distance. earlier: sealed before certificates carried them.

layer.description: The layer the whole compile stands on, as the certificate states it.

weakest.description: The weakest layer among its passes' checks, as the certificate states it.

whole.description: With partly: the check of the whole output against the whole program made here, its layer among it.

form.description: The receipt's form: rfc8785, or first.

given.description: How the job was given (section 9): its own text; its members, judged as the message wrote them; or a value already parsed, with no text to judge.

kind.description: The kind of answer the verifier judged it (WAI decision D164). job or set: a kind with no run again, whose verdict is its seal and every rule of the provider protocol's section 8.4, with what it works out again beside them (a sealed verdict, a compile's certificate, the equivalence checker's verdict); its figures are its host's word and are never run again. algorithm or estimate: an answer of a kind that is run again, here one whose receipt or rules failed, so it was not run again and is not valid. null: no kind could be told, and kind_refused says why; such an answer is never valid.

kind_refused.description: Why no kind could be told (D164): its result names a schema this verifier does not know; carries the engine's stamps apart, or an engine not of the form an engine writes; or is both an algorithm's answer and an estimate. The answer is not valid, whatever its seal.

not_seen.description: For a job given parsed: what parsing loses, which this verdict could not see.

planner.description: For a job under a contract, what its reasoning says: the route chosen, the class wanted and given, whether the choice depends on the host, what was kept, and the shadow.

provider.description: For a provider's result, what it says of itself.

reasons.description: Each rule the receipt breaks (the provider protocol's section 8.4, wasmq_form among them for a wasmQ job): none when it is valid.

time.description: What the receipt seals of when it was issued (the provider protocol's section 8.2), for a receipt of its form: the time, in milliseconds since 1970 by its signer's clock, or that it seals none.

not_after_ms.description: The first moment the receipt is no longer offered; null when it states none.

wasmq.description: For a wasmQ job (quantum-wasmq section 6.5), beside the verdict: how the run ended, each rule of the profile's form it breaks, and where the host's unsealed words differ from what is sealed, which change no verdict.

notes.description: Where the body's unsealed status or method differs from what is sealed or is missing, and members nothing seals: told beside the verdict, and no part of it.

outcome.description: The sealed result's status: ok, or fault.

problems.description: Each rule of quantum-wasmq section 6.5 the job breaks, in words (the reason wasmq_form): the first 64, then how many more. Empty when it breaks none.

anyOf.description: An estimate's check: its seal, every estimate's receipt, and the request re-run here giving the same figures.

checked_at_ms.description: With a time to hold the receipt to (section 8.8): that time.

given.description: From a surface that says how the job was given (the provider protocol's section 9): its own text; its members, judged as the message wrote them; or a value already parsed, with no text to judge.

kind.description: The kind of answer the verifier judged it (WAI decision D164): an estimate, run again.

not_seen.description: For a job given parsed: what parsing loses, which this verdict could not see.

reasons.description: The provider protocol's section 8.4 reasons: none, since an answer is run again only once its receipt and every rule hold; a receipt that fails is answered with its reasons alone.

rerun_error.description: Why the request could not be run again, when no host runs it (a request an estimate refuses): the answer is then not valid, and nothing is reproduced. Null when it ran.

skew_ms.description: How far after checked_at_ms a receipt's issue may be.

stamped.description: Whether the result carries the engine's stamps as every engine that made one wrote them (D164): format and schema are both wai.quantum.estimate/1, and engine an object whose name is wai-quantum and whose version is MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (with a pre-release or build where it has one). The run again leaves both out of what it compares (D158), and holds them to this all the same: an answer whose stamp is taken away or changed in form is not valid.

time.description: What the receipt seals of when it was issued (the provider protocol's section 8.2): the time, in milliseconds since 1970 by its signer's clock, or that it seals none.

not_after_ms.description: The first moment the receipt is no longer offered; null when it states none.

trust.description: With a trust list (section 8.8): whether it lists the receipt's key, and the window and revocation its entry gives.

anyOf.description: A set's check: the set's receipt over its request and head, the items the request gives at their indices, every item's own receipt, the root over the leaves and each item's path.

checked_at_ms.description: With a time to hold the receipt to (section 8.8): that time.

given.description: From a surface that says how the job was given (the provider protocol's section 9): its own text; its members, judged as the message wrote them; or a value already parsed, with no text to judge.

kind.description: Where a surface gives the set's verdict: the kind of answer the verifier judged it (WAI decision D164), set, a kind with no run again; null when no kind could be told (kind_refused says why), which is never valid.

kind_refused.description: Why no kind could be told (D164): its result names a schema this verifier does not know; carries the engine's stamps apart, or an engine not of the form an engine writes; or is both an algorithm's answer and an estimate. The answer is not valid, whatever its seal.

not_seen.description: For a job given parsed: what parsing loses, which this verdict could not see.

reasons.description: Each rule the set's receipt breaks (the provider protocol's sections 8.4 and 8.6): none when it is valid.

signer.description: That key as a did:key, where a surface gives it.

skew_ms.description: How far after checked_at_ms a receipt's issue may be.

time.description: What the set's receipt seals of when it was issued (the provider protocol's section 8.2): the time, in milliseconds since 1970 by its signer's clock, or that it seals none.

not_after_ms.description: The first moment the receipt is no longer offered; null when it states none.

trust.description: With a trust list (section 8.8): whether it lists the receipt's key, and the window and revocation its entry gives.

anyOf.description: Whether a result's receipt seals exactly that request and that result, and the key it names; for an estimate, also every estimate's receipt and the request re-run here; for a set, also every item's receipt, the root over them and each item's path.
A refusal as data: the message, every code in it (the last is the code), its outcome and meaning as the code's table gives them. A host that refuses for its own reasons gives the error alone.

outputSchema.description: Whether a result's receipt seals exactly that request and that result, and the key it names; for an estimate, also every estimate's receipt and the request re-run here; for a set, also every item's receipt, the root over them and each item's path.

title: Verify a result's receipt
